sourceScope: #85/#548/#606 describe interlocking programs, retaining fundamentals and choosing kettlebell days according to goals. Current-program scope, capacity accounting and the optional A/B/C switches are Strength Lab adaptations. No source-authored frequency or new minimum maintenance interval is asserted.
behavior: A/B/C prescription and capacity share their existing C-day selectors and equipment fallbacks. All reachable six-turn alternatives are considered, not only the current day.

Days containing only retired declared patterns no longer inflate recurrence distances between current-core visits. Mixed current work, partial current work and same-day grouping retain their physical scheduling meaning; every underlying actual receipt remains available to progression.

Switching off an optional C-day variant removes its historical recurrence from current core demand. Actual records and independent earned movement state remain intact; re-enabling recomputes demand from the same history.

Core attendance credit restarts after the latest actual day containing a retired declared A/B/C pattern. Partial physical work also resets this credit boundary; no actual record or earned progression is removed. This prevents old-program attendance surplus from postponing the current core. No rolling quota or new frequency formula is introduced.
Current core curriculum details and movement cadence use that same scope; an inactive core variant is not reported as a developing core requirement.

Selected pressing and other foundations, bodyweight fallback days and currently needed supporting prerequisites still contribute to real demand. Dedicated club/snatch/double programs retain their own existing scope regardless of the A/B/C style choice.
No movement is globally disabled by this scope repair. Actual unfinished work, equipment, skill, recovery, time, progression and storage contracts remain unchanged.

results.ordinaryComparisons: Six existing controlled/two-year 30/45/60-minute histories retain counts, qualification dates and earned progression. Core feedback now excludes inactive variants; output metadata is not claimed identical.
results.reproduceChangedGoal: node scripts/compare-core-scope.cjs /tmp/baseline-engine.js (export baseCommit engine.js with git show)

limitations: All ten gate areas remain unresolved. This is a false-overload repair, not automatic removal of a genuinely oversized core.
The controlled fixture is explicitly recorded prior work; it is not claimed to have been automatically generated within a 30-minute session.
A/B/C optional variants that remain enabled can still create high capacity demand. No uniform physiological frequency requirement is established.
Browser emulation does not replace physical Android or technique acceptance.

The changed-goal 120-workout diagnostic starts developing work March 4 instead of October 19 at 30 minutes, or April 13 at 45/60. Return counts increase 31 to 42, 18 to 19 and zero to nine respectively; several core endpoints qualify later. The 30-minute case earns seven core endpoints plus hinge practice versus six core endpoints and no developing endpoint. Wider admission and recurrence are not solved. All raw counts and dates are retained; this is an accounting repair rather than a claim of monotonic scheduling improvement.
General rolling-credit prototypes were rejected because they changed ordinary qualification outcomes. Only the current curriculum scope and its existing attendance-credit period are repaired.

verification.status: complete local regression; exact-head CI and live DEV verification follow push
verification.focused: Current scope, nine duration/frequency cases, reversible style/gear changes, partial pending work, retired-only days, correction/undo, future isolation, backup and immutable projections pass. Both mobile widths pass the new workflow.
verification.compatibility: 108 prescriptions unchanged; 432 complete plans match after allowing only the six expected inactive-circle core-feedback corrections. No other plan differences allowed.
verification.note: All suites passed across the broad run and final focused scope/credit/retired-only follow-ups. Browser group one resumed after the timer preference test was repaired and passed both widths; the earlier wave save wait passed the complete final rerun without weakened assertions. Generated audits remain reproducible.
